text: The Patriots are riding genuine momentum after Drake Maye's stunning rebound performance earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors—his three-touchdown display in the 29-26 victory over Buffalo marked the kind of clutch showing that Mike Vrabel emphasized as crucial for the defending AFC champs, though questions loom about whether this represents a genuine turnaround or another overreaction to a single impressive result. The roster situation has grown cloudier with Rhamondre Stevenson dealing with an injury that leaves the running back position in flux heading into Week 5, forcing the team to reassess depth at a position that figured prominently in their comebacks. The Raiders present a formidable defensive matchup, particularly in the secondary—while the Patriots successfully neutralized Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid last week, they'll face a sterner test against Las Vegas's 1-2 punch of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer at Gillette Stadium. Both Vrabel and Maye held press conferences this week to discuss the path forward, and the narrative seems clear: the Patriots have a genuine opportunity to validate their Week 4 resurgence, but it requires sustained execution rather than the kind of volatility that's defined their season so far.
